# Skill catalog

<!-- generated by `python -m omi skills`; do not edit -->
- write-skill (authoring): Use when creating or revising an omi-skill; gives the contract, trigger wording and acceptance test. [~713 tokens]
- docker-worker-pitfalls (delivery-ops): Use when an omi worker or run container fails, cannot write, cannot run git or the CLI, leaves containers or images behind, or when changing the worker Dockerfile. [~706 tokens]
- incident (delivery-ops): Use when something broke in a release, CI gate, ruleset, tag or worker run and you must triage, contain and record it. [~534 tokens]
- release-checklist (delivery-ops): Use when preparing, promoting or tagging a release (rc tag, development -> staging -> main PRs, v* tag) or checking a release PR before the PO tests it. [~653 tokens]
- rollback (delivery-ops): Use when a released candidate or main is bad and must be undone, by reverting the promotion merge or redeploying the previous rc tag. [~541 tokens]
- windows-powershell (delivery-ops): Use when running omi, git, gh, docker or shell scripts on Windows PowerShell or Git Bash, or when a command works on Linux but fails on the PO's Windows machine. [~554 tokens]
- ci-workflow-audit (quality): Use when adding or reviewing GitHub Actions workflows, especially those that run AI agents or act on pull requests from forks or issues. [~652 tokens]
- debug-root-cause (quality): Use when a test fails, a bug or unexpected behaviour appears, or a first fix did not work, before proposing any fix. [~588 tokens]
- diff-security-review (quality): Use when reviewing a code change for security regressions, especially auth, input handling, secrets, crypto or dependency changes. [~638 tokens]
- simplify-review (quality): Use when reviewing a diff for over-engineering, needless dependencies or speculative abstractions; lists what to cut. [~547 tokens]
- verify-evidence (quality): Use when about to say work is done, fixed or passing, before reporting DONE, committing or approving a review. [~537 tokens]
- brainstorm-ac (workflow): Use when a requirement or feature request is vague and must become testable acceptance criteria before a task file is written. [~618 tokens]
- change-request (workflow): Use when requirements, scope or an approved decision change after a task started, or an engineer reports NEEDS SCOPE. [~520 tokens]
- lean-implementation (workflow): Use when writing or fixing code and tempted to add abstractions, dependencies or config; keeps the diff minimal (YAGNI, stdlib first). [~571 tokens]
- task-brief (workflow): Use when a task file must be complete enough for a fresh engineer agent with zero context, before `omi run`. [~580 tokens]
